A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching distributions, benchmarks and experimental framework. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable and comparable. V2 includes Appendix A.1–A.6; v1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original tabular regression, MAESTRO prediction and image-generation experiments, including quantitative results in Tables 2–7.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 retain original experiments and add baseline and repeated-seed results. Appendix A also reports target-distribution analyses and additional generated examples.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 corrects the reported one-sided Dalap probability calculation: the denominator subtracts gamma^(mu+1), replacing gamma^(mu+2). The distribution families and network architectures remain intact. Newly documented Bitwise loss weighting does not independently establish a change to the previous implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Bicycles, Upvotes, Migration, MAESTRO, MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR10 for the same prediction tasks. Image reconstruction, conditional completion and unconditional generation are retained. The appendix analyzes existing coverage rather than introducing new datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add Poisson comparisons on Bicycles, Upvotes and MAESTRO. Tables 4 and 6 add categorical and single-component Dlogistic image comparisons; Dlogistic was already evaluated in mixture settings. These expand important comparator groups. Laplace becoming Dlaplace in the tabular tables is a naming change.

E3.justification: V1 Section 3.7 specifies a maximum gamma of 0.95 for Danorm in all experiments; v2 Appendix A.4 reports 1.0 for tabular and MAESTRO experiments. This revises a stated setting without establishing which experiments were rerun. Existing splits, architectures, training budgets and evaluation metrics otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 adds systematic target-distribution analysis through summary statistics, histograms and dispersion comparisons, extending v1's tabular descriptions. Section 5.1 adds an initialization-failure analysis: two Dalap Migration runs diverge, whereas mixtures converge across seeds. Appendix A.2 expands qualitative examples, including previously unillustrated Dnormal and Laplace outputs.

E5.justification: V1 reports seed 42 throughout. V2 introduces ten-seed means and standard errors with fixed datasets, revealing substantial variability in some tabular results. It also states ten-seed reporting for MAESTRO, although those table columns omit standard errors. Image experiments remain single-run, now with an explicit uncertainty limitation.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 replace tabular single-run results with seed aggregates and change rankings. For example, non-mixture Dalap on Migration changes from 22.80 bits to 2.9e5 ± 1.9e5; these are different reporting conditions, not a direct performance deterioration. Poisson's 4.91 MAESTRO bits and categorical/single-component Dlogistic image results are newly reported. Existing image-method scores are retained.

T1.justification: V2 removes the discretized-Laplace gradient formulas, corrects Dalap normalization and expectation algebra, rewrites the Danorm expectation proof, and revises Bitwise proofs. Appendix A.3 introduces a formal analysis of changes in the complete Dalap loss. These substantially revise mathematical reasoning beyond notation or relocation, although some new steps contain errors.

C1.justification: The research objective and abstract remain stable. The introduction and conclusion shift from jointly recommending Dalap and Bitwise toward Dalap as the general recommendation, reserving Bitwise and Dnormal for extreme dispersion and acknowledging Poisson's MAESTRO result. V2 also limits its performance positioning to the evaluated comparisons.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking distribution choice to data characteristics, Dalap initialization failures and mixture stabilization. It replaces the claimed Dweib convergence failure on Migration with an unsupported-target explanation and explicitly qualifies single-run image evidence. Appendix A.3 reverses v1's interpretation of the isolated regularization term and considers its interaction with the full loss.

D1.justification: Appendices A.4–A.6 document parameter activations, numerical caps, Dalap boundary handling, Weibull forward/backward pseudocode and positional Bitwise loss weighting. These substantially expand implementation disclosure without proving corresponding implementation changes. The repository link is retained, a module location is added, and v1's named compute-cluster acknowledgments are removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Cover, Ho et al., Dhariwal and Nichol, Radford et al., and Rybkin et al., expanding the information-theoretic motivation and explaining the focus on likelihood-based models rather than diffusion. The computing-infrastructure citation is removed. Most related work and original method attribution remain unchanged; NETtalk's author information is a metadata correction.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten, replacing the opening MIDI example with broader integer-regression motivation and a flight-control example. Results and conclusions are substantially revised, subsection organization is expanded, and loss discussion moves into a structured appendix. Author affiliation/contact text and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different document template, typography and text width. Comparison tables gain baseline rows and uncertainty displays; new tables, distribution plots and sample panels expand the visual material. V1 Figure 2 becomes Appendix Figure 13 with a revised caption, while the original main image examples are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: New baselines and ten-seed tabular results strengthen the evidence, expose Dalap's initialization failures and support more qualified recommendations. Normalization corrections and implementation disclosures also help. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: MAESTRO lacks the stated uncertainty display, and some rankings in the prose contradict Tables 2–3 and 6. Added technical material also contains errors, including incorrect algebra in Appendix A.3 and log(expm1(diff)) for nonpositive diff in the Weibull pseudocode.
